name: Kotak Mahindra Bank Ltd
title: Kotak Mahindra Bank Ltd - 500247 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Kotak's Q2 was flattered by a one-off INR55,344 crore FCNR(B) inflow that lifted deposits, while core advances grew 19% YoY and NIM fell 22 bps QoQ to 4.31%; credit cost eased to 0.35%.

summary.headline: Kotak Q2FY27 consolidated PAT rose 26% YoY to INR 5,645 crore, helped by INR 55,344 crore FCNR(B) mobilisation and lower credit cost of 35 bps.
summary.overview: Bank standalone PAT was INR 4,212 crore, up 29% YoY, with Q2 PBT of INR 5,579 crore. Net advances grew 25% YoY, but core growth excluding FCNR(B)-linked loans and the KMIL transferred book was 19% YoY. Net interest margin fell 22 bps QoQ to 4.31%, with FCNR(B) and related advances contributing 15 bps, and management said the mobilised FCNR(B) funds will be deployed over the next few quarters. Asset quality improved on all parameters, with gross NPA at 1.04% and credit cost at 35 bps versus 46 bps in Q1. Subsidiaries contributed 26% of consolidated PAT, hit by market-linked MTM losses.

segments.name: Bank standalone
segments.commentary: PAT INR 4,212 crore (+29% YoY). Balance sheet about INR 9 lakh crore; NII +16% YoY; non-interest income +23% YoY (+17% excluding processing fee on FCNR(B)-linked advances).

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Combined PAT INR 1,450 crore (+18% YoY), 26% of consolidated PAT, hit by negative MTM on equity and yield movements. Kotak Securities PAT INR 348 crore vs INR 345 crore; Kotak AMC PAT INR 287 crore (+11%); KAAML PAT INR 87 crore; Kotak Prime PAT INR 251 crore (+2%); Kotak Life shareholders' PAT INR 198 crore.

segments.name: Corporate bank and SME
segments.commentary: Corporate bank loans +25% YoY (+17% ex-KMIL book); corporate bank fee income +36% YoY, 20% of Bank fee income. SME advances +27% YoY to about INR 1.4 lakh crore (24% of advances), with INR 11,200 crore ECLGS sanctioned.

segments.name: Retail and unsecured
segments.commentary: Unsecured retail share 8.1% of advances; absolute unsecured growth INR 1,730 crore vs INR 707 crore in Q1. Mortgage +14% YoY; CV/CE +8% YoY to over INR 47,000 crore; tractor loans +11% YoY; retail microcredit +18% YoY; credit card portfolio +7% YoY.

guidance_outlook: FCNR(B) funds of about INR 55,000 crore to be deployed into customer assets over the next few quarters, in addition to core growth.
Management targets advances growth of 1.5x to 2x nominal GDP; no capital or liquidity constraint cited.

NIM to reflect full-quarter FCNR(B) impact, offset by progressive deployment and repo transmission on floating-rate loans; repo impact to start from October and be fully felt in Q4. Management declined to give margin guidance.
One-time ECL transition impact on 1 April expected to be less than 2% of net worth; recurring credit cost impact of 12-15 bps previously flagged, with clarity expected in Q3.
Technology to remain about 13% of total opex; no forward opex or cost-to-assets guidance given.
capex_capacity: KMIL loan portfolio of about INR 9,600 crore transferred to the Bank in early July 2026 following an RBI circular on same-business-in-multiple-entities; KMIL will not be an operating entity going forward.
FCNR(B) mobilisation of USD 5.78 billion (INR 55,344 crore), about 9.7% of June deposit base; INR 16,100 crore of loans given against FCNR(B) deposits; INR 9,800 crore net IBPC repayment.
Gold loan automation process delivered; hybrid home loan launched; Fyn corporate portal onboarding up 34% YoY and active base up about 60%.
demand_pricing: Average deposits +19% YoY and +8% QoQ; current accounts +17% YoY and fixed-rate SA +14% YoY (averages). Ex-FCNR(B) period-end deposits +13% YoY; CASA ex-FCNR(B) 41.8% vs 40.3% in June.
Loan book: about 60% repo-linked and 65-70% floating, per management.

Unsecured: personal loans and business loans +9% YoY; credit card spends +8.9% YoY, portfolio +7% YoY; microcredit +18% YoY. Tractor delinquencies not yet impacted, but management is watching a 13% monsoon rainfall deficit.
Trade and supply chain finance grew strongly; UPI issuer market share 3.8%; NACH market share up 300 bps; UPI acquiring up 5x YoY.
Investment banking strong on rebound in primary markets; cross-selling of IB and institutional brokerage added about 109 bps to corporate banking RoE. Custody balances hit by muted FII flows.

qa_highlights.question: What is the P&L impact of KMIL, and how much of the FCNR(B) money is still to be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said KMIL loans transferred in early July and their NII is booked in the Bank with no interest expense at KMIL; KMIL's standard provision release is booked in the Bank, with no consolidated impact. Management said the undeployed FCNR(B) funds will be deployed over the next few quarters, in addition to core deposit-led growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will NIM recover from Q4 after the Q3 dip?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said repo transmission on floating-rate loans starts October, full effect in Q4, and that deployment of funds takes about three months. Management declined to give margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How should opex growth be viewed going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management divided opex into acquisition costs (which it will grow), technology (about 13% of opex, expected to stay there), and marketing (to grow), while fixed overheads and manual processes will be cut. No quantified opex growth guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is unsecured growth sustainable at about INR 1,700-1,800 crore a quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Saha said growth will be granular, focused on existing customers, with no rush. He attributed the earlier personal loan volatility to the run-off of an inorganic StanC portfolio, which is now almost gone. New term loan and overdraft products are being offered; they are still nascent.

risks_watch: NIM trajectory in Q3: FCNR(B) full-quarter cost versus deployment pace and repo transmission.
Pace of deployment of about INR 55,000 crore FCNR(B) funds into customer assets, and whether core growth holds above 19%.
Recurring ECL-related credit cost (12-15 bps previously flagged) and one-time transition impact (under 2% of net worth) pending RBI clarity in Q3.
Tractor and rural credit exposure given a 13% monsoon rainfall deficit and El Nino concerns.
Subsidiary earnings volatility from market-linked MTM and muted FII flows affecting custody.
Cost-to-assets trajectory: 2.40% in Q2 without forward guidance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on franchise, asset quality and cost trends, but deliberately non-committal on margins, opex and ECL impact. Management was evasive on treasury yields for parked FCNR(B) liquidity and declined to give margin or opex guidance.
key_quotes: We believe that the FCNR(B) program is a one-off opportunity.
We are confident in our ability to deliver responsible and profitable growth.
We really don't provide margin guidance.

growth.why: Management targets advances growth of 1.5x to 2x nominal GDP and says ~INR 55,000 crore of FCNR(B) funds will be deployed over the next few quarters, with INR 16,100 crore already lent against them; no capacity additions or specific order book were cited, and no margin guidance was given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM fell 22 bps QoQ to 4.31% with FCNR(B) and related advances costing 15 bps; repo transmission on ~60% repo-linked loans starts October and is fully felt in Q4, but management declined to give margin guidance and deployment of INR 55,344 crore FCNR(B) funds takes about three months.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new branches, plants or capacity additions were discussed; the KMIL book of about INR 9,600 crore was transferred into the Bank rather than adding capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets advances growth of 1.5x to 2x nominal GDP; core growth ex-FCNR(B) and KMIL was 19% YoY, and INR 16,100 crore is already lent against FCNR(B) with the balance to be deployed over the next few quarters.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the brief gives no utilisation figure and no board plan for new investment.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to give margin or opex guidance and only held its existing advances-growth philosophy, so there is no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The recurring ECL credit cost uplift of 12-15 bps is still pending RBI clarity in Q3, and the NIM path depends on FCNR(B) full-quarter cost versus deployment pace.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Hybrid home loan launched and new term loan and overdraft products for unsecured customers are being offered, but they are described as nascent with no quantified targets.

rows.label: FCNR(B) fund deployment into customer assets
rows.why: About INR 55,000 crore of FCNR(B) funds to be deployed, with INR 16,100 crore already lent against them, so loan growth should rise above core growth of 19% YoY.

rows.label: Opex mix shift and overhead cuts
rows.why: Cost-to-assets fell to 2.40% from 2.66% in Q1 and cost-to-income is 45.2%, down 160 bps YoY; management will grow acquisition and marketing spend while cutting fixed overheads, but gave no quantified guidance.

rows.label: RBI clarity on ECL transition and recurring credit cost
rows.why: One-time ECL transition impact is expected under 2% of net worth and the 12-15 bps recurring credit cost uplift awaits RBI clarity in Q3.

tone.note: Management was confident on franchise, asset quality (GNPA 1.04%, credit cost 35 bps) and cost trends, but declined to give margin, opex or ECL guidance and was evasive on treasury yields for parked FCNR(B) liquidity; analysts pressed on NIM recovery in Q4 and on sustainability of unsecured growth.

oneOffs.what: Net advances +25% YoY headline vs 19% core growth excluding FCNR(B)-linked loans and the KMIL transferred book
INR 55,344 crore FCNR(B) mobilisation inflow flatters deposit growth; ex-FCNR(B) period-end deposits +13% YoY
Q2FY26 credit cost of 79 bps versus 35 bps now; lower credit cost lifts profit growth, though it is not a revenue one-off

quality.why: Headline net advances +25% YoY and PAT +29% (standalone) are flattered by FCNR(B)-linked loans and the KMIL transfer; core growth ex these is 19% YoY and ex-FCNR(B) deposits grew 13%, while lower credit cost (35 bps vs 79 bps a year ago) lifted profit growth.
